`specs/minds-eval-harbor/outcome_verification.md` no longer describes the pre-existing set's second half as the workspace's `system/supervisord.conf` catted on its own. That half is now the whole supervisord config -- the main file plus every drop-in under `system/supervisord.conf.d/` -- because a workspace template is free to declare each program in its own drop-in, and the default template does. The accounting the spec describes is unchanged: the same join through the config's `forward_port.py` invocations, over more files.

It also records what the capture now does when it could not read that config whole. supervisord runs what its config declares, so a `supervisorctl status` listing that names programs while the captured config declares no supervised section is a read that missed part of the config; the pre-existing set is then unknown rather than one that quietly omits a template app, and a row whose owning program could not be resolved scores `error` with reason `supervisord_conf_unreadable` rather than `failed` with `no_supervised_program`.
